CVE-2026-116779.title: FreeSWITCH: Inbound SIP MESSAGE can select the api chat proto and run FreeSWITCH API commands
CVE-2026-116779.description: FreeSWITCH is a Software Defined Telecom Stack enabling the digital transformation from proprietary telecom switches to a software implementation that runs on any commodity hardware. Prior to 1.11.3, sofia_presence_handle_sip_i_message() split the To user of an inbound SIP MESSAGE on a plus sign and treated the left side as a chat protocol selector. Selecting the api chat proto reached switch_api_execute(), allowing a peer whose MESSAGE was accepted to run FreeSWITCH API commands, including operating-system command sinks, with the daemon's privileges. Inbound chat is enabled on the stock internal and external profiles, and any authenticated profile account is sufficient; stock directory users without password material can also remove that barrier in affected configurations. The flaw permits configuration and credential disclosure, arbitrary call control, and command execution, and exploitation has been observed in the wild. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.3.

CVE-2026-98578.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nfc: st21nfca: validate ISO15693 inventory length

The ISO15693 inventory helper removes a two-byte prefix without checking
that it exists, then accepts a one-byte remainder before reading data[1] as
the DSFID.

Require the prefix and at least two remaining bytes before copying the UID
data and reading the DSFID.

CVE-2026-98592.title: net: spacemit: clear TX descriptor on fragment mapping failure
CVE-2026-98592.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: spacemit: clear TX descriptor on fragment mapping failure

emac_tx_mem_map() writes TX_DESC_0_OWN into the ring descriptor for
every slot beyond old_head as soon as that slot's memset()'d local
copy is committed with "*tx_desc_addr = tx_desc", i.e. before the
buffers for that slot have necessarily all been mapped successfully.
If emac_tx_map_frag() then fails on a later fragment, the err_free_skb
path calls emac_free_tx_buf() to unmap and drop the skb, but leaves
the already-written descriptor memory untouched, and tx_ring->head is
never advanced past old_head (the "tx_ring->head = head" store is
skipped by the goto).

So a slot between old_head and the rolled-back head can be left with
TX_DESC_0_OWN set and buffer_addr_{1,2} pointing at DMA mappings that
emac_free_tx_buf() just tore down, while software considers that slot
free again. The next successful emac_tx_mem_map() call only rebuilds
old_head itself; if…

CVE-2026-98660.title: iio: pressure: bmp280: fix out-of-bounds access in sampling frequency lookup
CVE-2026-98660.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

iio: pressure: bmp280: fix out-of-bounds access in sampling frequency lookup

The sampling frequency tables store each frequency as an integer part and
a fractional part in micro units. num_sampling_freq_avail is initialized
to the number of flattened integer elements because read_avail() returns
the table as a flat array.

bmp280_write_sampling_frequency(), however, indexes the same table as a
two-dimensional array and uses num_sampling_freq_avail as the number of
rows. Convert the flattened element count back to the number of rows
before iterating over the table.

CVE-2026-98875.title: drm/nouveau/gsp: add SEC2 to GA100 chip table
CVE-2026-98875.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/nouveau/gsp: add SEC2 to GA100 chip table

The booter-load and booter-unload firmware run on the SEC2 falcon.
During tu102_gsp_oneinit(), the booter constructor needs device->sec2
to access the SEC2 falcon.

Without the .sec2 entry, device->sec2 is NULL and this dereference
crashes during GSP-RM boot.
